CONTEXT: two small yes/no classifier questions decide whether the engine refuses a command that moves a fixed thing, and whether it adds a clarification sentence. A live run found two misses: (1) relocates_thing answered no to a repositioning command ("Tilt the workstation onto its side."); (2) names_other_action answered no to a shared-verb command where one verb covers two objects ("Carry the driver's seat and my laptop into the kitchen."). This is the ONE tuning pass; wording only, no logic changes.

BUILD (plain 12th-grade words, one idea per sentence, like the existing text):
1. relocates_thing: add to the instructions list of what relocating means: tilts it, tips it over, rotates it, turns it around, rolls it, nudges it, shifts it, or repositions it. In the true criterion keep it short. In the false criterion add one plain sentence that a part used as designed is not relocating the thing: a door swung open or shut, a drawer slid open or shut, a lid opened, or a screen tilted back on its own hinge. Do not remove any existing wording.
2. names_other_action: in the instructions and/or the true criterion, add one plain sentence that a second object joined by "and" counts as something other than moving these fixed things, even when one verb covers both objects (use the exact phrase "one verb" in the text). Use only your own invented example, such as "Carry the crate and my bag outside."
3. Do NOT put any of these commands anywhere in source or tests (a check greps for them): Drag the workstation and my laptop; Lift the passenger seat and the back door; Push the driver's seat and my laptop; Rotate the workstation, then; Turn the workstation around; Reposition the passenger seat.; Roll the workstation toward; Nudge the back door; Swing the back door open; Press on the drawer to check; Tilt my laptop screen back; Slide the drawer open, then close.

TESTS in tests/test_fixed_refusal.py (hermetic, fake classifier): add test_relocates_thing_wording_covers_repositioning_and_use (the payload instructions mention tilt, rotate, roll, nudge and reposition and the false criterion mentions a door swung or a drawer slid) and test_names_other_action_wording_covers_shared_verb (the payload text contains "one verb"). Keep every existing test passing.

Lint: `.../python -m ruff check <files>` and `-m ruff format <files>`.

HARD RULES: wording only; no regex over narration; the notes file must list the exact new sentences and any assumption.
